A curiously common sight in the many rivers throughout the Tanglewood, the peaceful gurabara float down the streams chewing 
on reed and river fruit along the sun dappled water in absolute contentment. Numerous predators, often prowling right next to the 
drowsy beasts, barely spare them a glance as they rush down their game trails to savage far more diffi cult prey. While not impervious to 
the sudden snapping mandibles of a korrask or the wide ranging slaughter of a nicalliath, the gurubara still remain rather safe in their 
lackadaisical lifestyle. Th e key to this mysterious protection is the aquatic algae that proliferates within their fur and stains it a healthy 
green. Calming pheromones wafts from the algae, cooling tempers and the pangs of hunger of nearby predators.

Encountering Often found near the streams and rivers that cut 
through the Wealdwoods, the gurubara herds, numbering in 
a little over two dozen, float aimlessly, basking in the sun that 
breaks through the gloom, munching on aquatic plants. While 
there is no effort into approaching them, refraining from the 
urge to lie by the rivers edge or float alongside them, becomes 
a feeling more diffi cult to resist than a Traveler would expect.
